extract.why: The served transcription is the shelf's TWO volume transcriptions of Taylor's 1816 edition, concatenated: vol. I entire, then vol. II over the lines the Theology of Plato occupies in it. It is not a fresh transcription. The work stops where vol. II's own second work begins (the Elements of Theology, which has its own edition in this library), not where the treatises begin -- the measurement is recorded in scan.json, and the reasoning in edition.json.source_edition.statement.

sources.role: vol. I, the work entire (printed pp. 1-425)
vol. II, the Theology of Plato alone (printed pp. 1-299)
sources.stops: The Theology's last text line is vol. II line 40786, the close of CHAP. LI (printed page 299). Vol. II's next work begins at line 40813 -- the Elements of Theology, Proposition I -- and the treatises (On Providence and Fate, whose text opens at line 58122; the Ten Doubts concerning Providence; the Subsistence of Evil) follow the Elements. Neither is cut from this source: the Elements has its own edition here, and the treatises are outside the work.
